items.title: Knives and poison within reach of kids, prompting closure of day care centre
items.description: Three early learning services, including one at an elite private school, will be closed down today as part of a national push to lift quality.

items.title: Capital gains tax reform among options as Labor weighs housing pitch
items.description: After Jim Chalmers repeatedly refused to rule out changing the capital gains tax discount, a government source told the ABC that changes related to housing were being considered, with capital gains not ruled out.

items.title: Live: Wong responds to call for Australia to arrest Israeli president
items.description: Australian human rights lawyer Chris Sidoti has called for Israeli President Isaac Herzog to be arrested in Australia for inciting genocide. Follow live.

items.title: Report points to Pacific Islander exploitation
items.description: Changing jobs is a basic right for most people, but it is not so simple for Pacific Australia Labour Mobility workers.

items.title: Inquest findings for Westfield Bondi Junction today, after delay
items.description: Findings from the coronial inquest into the Westfield Bondi Junction stabbing will be handed down today.

items.title: The $120m airport and $550m highway built for Timor-Leste's boom that never came
items.description: The Greater Sunrise gas project was meant to transform Timor-Leste and bring billions in revenue, but locals are still waiting for the jobs and opportunities that were promised.

items.title: Corruption body chief asked to explain himself after Defence ties emerged
items.description: Attorney-General Michelle Rowland asked Paul Brereton to explain why his ongoing ties to Defence had not been "adequately" disclosed in a letter sent last year.

items.title: How a teenager who failed swimming lessons pulled off miracle ocean rescue
items.description: Austin Appelbee, 13, has made international headlines after swimming for four hours in rough seas to save his mum, sister and brother stranded in the ocean. How did he do it?

items.title: Ex-prince Andrew leaves Windsor home after latest Epstein revelations
items.description: British police are investigating Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor after new files suggest Jeffrey Epstein arranged for a woman to have sex with the former prince at his home at the Royal Lodge in 2010.

items.title: Man accused of pretending to shoot from Bondi bridge to face court
items.description: A man accused of mimicking firing on people near the pedestrian bridge where the Bondi terror attack occurred is due to face court.

items.title: Online safety watchdog says tech giants failing to detect child abuse
items.description: Major tech companies including Apple, Google, Meta and Microsoft are still failing to do enough to detect and stop child sexual abuse, eSafety has claimed.

items.title: Live: AUD touching 70 US cents while Wall Street dips on AI stocks
items.description: Follow the day's events and insights as they happen with our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Trump's border tsar says 700 ICE agents will leave Minnesota
items.description: The administration's border tsar says the decision came after local and state authorities agreed to cooperate more closely with its immigration crackdown.

items.title: Body-worn camera footage shows moment grandmother removed from birth suite
items.description: A confrontation caught on body-worn security footage in the halls of the Toowoomba Hospital maternity unit highlights concerns raised by local mothers.

items.title: FOI documents reveal how Anika Wells's New York trip costs escalated
items.description: The final New York travel bill for Communications Minister Anika Wells and her staffer rose $7,000 from an initial booking due to last-minute changes.

items.title: Fears for thousands of renters as rental affordability scheme ends
items.description: Vulnerable and elderly residents in homes subsidised by the National Rental Affordability Scheme are staring down decade-long waitlists for social housing as the scheme draws to a close.

items.title: Quiz: How much do you know about the Winter Olympics?
items.description: The Winter Olympics gets underway in Milan Cortina this week — but how much do you know about the Winter Olympics? Test yourself in our fiendish quiz.

items.title: Two months into the social media ban and teenagers say it isn't working
items.description: Australia's world-first social media ban for under-16s is two months old, but teenagers say they have found ways around it.

items.title: Report says Australia's focus on China has 'eroded' Taiwan's trust
items.description: Experts say Australia needs to do more to grow its relationship with Taiwan as China works to diplomatically isolate Taipei in the region.

items.title: What is the difference between tropical low and cyclone?
items.description: Tropical lows are weaker than tropical cyclones, but a meteorologist explains they can still cause significant damage.

items.title: Police investigating second 'vile' letter sent to Sydney mosque
items.description: It is the second such incident in the past 10 days after police charged a 70-year-old man with allegedly sending a threatening letter to Lakemba Mosque in late January.

items.title: Seven killed in Russian attacks in Ukraine as peace talks resume
items.description: Another round of US-brokered talks on ending the almost four-year war began as Russian cluster munitions killed seven people at a market in Ukraine.

items.title: Man who tried to assassinate Donald Trump jailed for life
items.description: Ryan Routh will spend the rest of his life behind bars for his 2024 assassination attempt on the then US presidential hopeful.

items.title: Streaky Bay takes shark safety into its own hands after fatal attacks
items.description: Nine volunteers in Streaky Bay are now qualified drone pilots and can be called upon for coastal surveillance or emergencies.

items.title: Calls for more detail on coal mine water releases into reef catchment
items.description: There were 55 water releases from the region's coal mines in the month of January into the largest catchment draining to the Great Barrier Reef.
